name: Andromeda Galaxy
description: The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way, and the most distant object easily visible to the naked eye.

name: Triangulum Galaxy
description: The third-largest member of the Local Group, with loosely wound arms rich in star-forming regions.

name: Sculptor Galaxy
description: A dusty starburst spiral and one of the brightest galaxies in the sky outside the Local Group.

name: Skull Nebula
description: A mottled planetary nebula surrounding a central pair of stars, giving it a hollow, skull-like glow.

name: NGC 300
description: A quiet, isolated spiral on the edge of the Sculptor Group, notable for how evenly its star formation is spread across its disc.

name: NGC 772
description: An unbarred spiral with one noticeably extended arm, likely drawn out by a smaller companion galaxy.

name: NGC 891
description: An edge-on spiral often described as a near-twin of the Milky Way, split by a dust lane knotted with star-forming clouds.

name: M77
description: A nearby spiral with an actively feeding supermassive black hole, one of the closest and most studied Seyfert galaxies.

name: NGC 1097
description: A barred spiral with faint, wispy jets extending from its nucleus, thought to be the shredded remains of a small companion galaxy.

name: NGC 1300
description: A large barred spiral seen nearly face-on, its central bar funneling gas toward the galaxy's core.

name: Crab Nebula
description: The wreckage of a star that was seen to explode in the year 1054 CE, now a fast-expanding cloud of glowing gas around a central pulsar. Lies close to the Galactic plane, so imagery from this survey layer may be limited.

name: Orion Nebula
description: A vast stellar nursery visible to the naked eye, one of the closest regions of active star formation to Earth. Lies close to the Galactic plane, so imagery from this survey layer may be limited.

name: UFO Galaxy
description: A tightly wound, nearly edge-on spiral whose elongated silhouette earned it an unofficial nickname.

name: NGC 2903
description: A bright barred spiral with an active burst of star formation packed into its central region.

name: Bode's Galaxy
description: A grand-design spiral and one of the closest large galaxies to the Milky Way.

name: Cigar Galaxy
description: A starburst galaxy undergoing an intense burst of star formation, with outflows of hot gas streaming from its disc.

name: Spindle Galaxy
description: An edge-on lenticular galaxy shaped like a spindle, with a dense, unusually massive central black hole for its size.

name: M95
description: A tightly barred spiral with an inner ring of star formation encircling its nucleus.

name: M96
description: The brightest member of the M96 Group, with an asymmetric spiral structure likely shaped by past interactions.

name: M105
description: A smooth, featureless elliptical galaxy, a textbook example of the type.

name: M108
description: A nearly edge-on barred spiral with a mottled, patchy disc and no visible central bulge.

name: M65
description: One-third of the Leo Triplet, a spiral with a smooth disc and relatively little visible dust.

name: M66
description: The largest member of the Leo Triplet, with an asymmetric spiral structure shaped by gravitational interaction with its neighbors.

name: NGC 3628
description: The third member of the Leo Triplet, seen exactly edge-on with a prominent warped dust lane.

name: M109
description: A barred spiral with faint, extended arms, one of the more distant Messier galaxies.

name: Antennae Galaxies
description: Two spiral galaxies caught mid-collision, their stars flung into long tidal tails by the encounter.

name: M98
description: A highly inclined spiral in the Virgo Cluster, its light dimmed somewhat by dust along its disc.

name: M99
description: An asymmetric spiral with one noticeably longer arm, likely disturbed by a recent close pass with another galaxy.

name: M106
description: A spiral galaxy whose central black hole mass was one of the first measured precisely, using water masers orbiting its core.

name: M61
description: A large, actively star-forming barred spiral and one of the biggest members of the Virgo Cluster.

name: M100
description: A grand-design spiral in the Virgo Cluster with two prominent, well-defined arms.

name: M84
description: A lenticular-leaning elliptical galaxy near the core of the Virgo Cluster, with jets of radio-emitting plasma from its nucleus.

name: M85
description: One of the brightest galaxies in the Virgo Cluster, showing faint shell-like structures thought to be the aftermath of a past merger.

name: M86
description: One of the largest galaxies in the Virgo Cluster, moving toward us faster than almost any other known galaxy relative to the Milky Way.

name: NGC 4449
description: A small, boxy irregular galaxy undergoing a vigorous burst of star formation across its whole disc.

name: M49
description: The brightest galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, a massive elliptical thought to anchor its own subgroup within the cluster.

name: M87
description: A giant elliptical at the heart of the Virgo Cluster, home to the black hole first imaged directly by the Event Horizon Telescope.

name: M88
description: A well-defined spiral on the outskirts of the Virgo Cluster, tilted at an angle that shows off its arm structure clearly.

name: M91
description: A barred spiral in the Virgo Cluster, historically one of the more difficult Messier objects to pin down due to a cataloging mix-up.

name: M89
description: A nearly spherical elliptical galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, surrounded by a faint, extended envelope of stars.

name: Needle Galaxy
description: One of the sky's most striking edge-on spirals, sliced through the middle by a thin, dark dust lane.

name: M90
description: A spiral galaxy moving so fast relative to the Virgo Cluster's center that it may eventually be flung out of the cluster entirely.

name: M58
description: A barred spiral with a bright, active nucleus, among the largest galaxies in the Virgo Cluster.

name: Sombrero Galaxy
description: A nearly edge-on spiral with an unusually large central bulge and a sharp, dark dust lane, giving it the silhouette of a wide-brimmed hat.

name: M59
description: A moderately flattened elliptical galaxy in the Virgo Cluster, orbited by a rich system of globular clusters.

name: M60
description: One of the most massive galaxies in the Virgo Cluster, paired visually with the smaller spiral NGC 4647 nearby.

name: Mice Galaxies
description: A pair of colliding spiral galaxies stretched into long, thin tidal tails by their mutual gravity.

name: M94
description: A compact spiral with a bright inner ring of star formation encircling its nucleus.

name: Black Eye Galaxy
description: A spiral galaxy with a striking dark band of dust across its bright nucleus, likely the result of an ancient merger.

name: Sunflower Galaxy
description: A bright spiral with tightly wound, dusty arms radiating outward like petals.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy
description: A grand-design spiral locked in a slow gravitational dance with its smaller companion, NGC 5195.

name: Pinwheel Galaxy
description: A large, face-on spiral with sweeping, asymmetric arms studded with star-forming regions.

name: NGC 5548
description: A well-studied Seyfert galaxy whose actively accreting black hole has been monitored for decades.

name: M102
description: A disc galaxy seen edge-on, split by a dust lane; its identification with Messier's original observation of M102 is still debated.

name: Great Hercules Cluster
description: One of the brightest globular clusters visible from the northern hemisphere, containing several hundred thousand stars bound tightly by gravity.

name: NGC 6503
description: A small, isolated spiral sitting at the edge of a vast, otherwise empty region of space called the Local Void.

name: Cat's Eye Nebula
description: A planetary nebula with an intricate, layered structure of shells and knots, from a complex history of outbursts from its central star.

name: Ring Nebula
description: A glowing shell of gas cast off by a dying star, forming the ring shape that made it one of the first planetary nebulae ever discovered.

name: Dumbbell Nebula
description: One of the brightest planetary nebulae in the sky, its double-lobed shape formed as a dying star's outer layers expanded outward.

name: Fireworks Galaxy
description: A face-on spiral nicknamed for the unusually high number of supernovae observed within it over the past century.

name: NGC 7217
description: A quiet, symmetric spiral with multiple concentric rings of stars thought to trace a history of past minor mergers.

name: Helix Nebula
description: One of the closest planetary nebulae to Earth, formed by a dying sun-like star shedding its outer layers into space.

name: NGC 7331
description: Sometimes called a twin of the Milky Way in size and structure, anchoring a small group of more distant background galaxies.

name: NGC 7793
description: A flocculent spiral in the Sculptor Group, with short, patchy arm segments rather than one continuous spiral pattern.
